answer: A glacier-fed saffron farm pays agents to operate prism sensors. Each certified sensor has an immutable serial and a non-exportable signing key. Fresh nonce signatures prove possession; a ledger pays at most one reward per serial per time slot, including after certificate renewal or account-key changes. Aliases or relayed proofs from one device share that limit. An attacker seeking n rewards in one slot must buy or rent n genuine sensors. Trust rests on the issuer binding one serial to each physical device and on keys resisting cloning; hardware-rich operators can still dominate.
